body:
Please leave your feedback about new 'mini.map' module here. Feel free to either add new comment or positively upvote existing one.

Some things I am interested to find out (obviously, besides bugs):

- Are configuration and function names intuitive enough?
- Are default values of settings convenient for you?
- Is documentation and examples clear enough?

Thanks!

2. Behaviour with file explorer open on the right side (NvimTree)

> First time around here. In case I miss some conventions or am following an anti-pattern, please do call it out.

Welcome!

This is probably an issue with terminal emulator and font combination. Could you paste these characters as a plain text in the buffer and tell me what you see (screenshot would be nice):
```
  ' ', '🬀', '🬁', '🬂', '🬃', '🬄', '🬅', '🬆', '🬇', '🬈', '🬉', '🬊', '🬋', '🬌', '🬍', '🬎',

  '🬞', '🬟', '🬠', '🬡', '🬢', '🬣', '🬤', '🬥', '🬦', '🬧', '▐', '🬨', '🬩', '🬪', '🬫', '🬬',
  '🬭', '🬮', '🬯', '🬰', '🬱', '🬲', '🬳', '🬴', '🬵', '🬶', '🬷', '🬸', '🬹', '🬺', '🬻', '█',
```

On a similar note, how about these characters:
```
'⣤', '⣥', '⣬', '⣭', '⣦', '⣧', '⣮', '⣯', '⣴', '⣵', '⣼', '⣽', '⣶', '⣷', '⣾', '⣿',
```

If they are not displayed correctly (as blocks and braille dots) in normal buffer, then there is not much I can you with here. Maybe try other terminal emulator (kitty, maybe).

Ah, so the first set of characters are all confused boxes (apart from 2 characters),
The 2nd set though seems to render fine.

![Screenshot 2022-10-12 at 10 27 43 AM](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/16442535/195253770-9fe852cf-47f3-4527-8f55-87a9d0cde4bb.png)

Seems to work fine with Kitty, though the interaction with NvimTree still seems a bit wonky
![Screenshot 2022-10-12 at 10 34 24 AM](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/16442535/195254603-f636cbf8-794e-471c-85ce-36a050e07996.png)

I think ideally the map should offset the tree or get offsetted by it instead of getting overlapped

> Ah, so the first set of characters are all confused boxes (apart from 2 characters), The 2nd set though seems to render fine.
> 
> ![Screenshot 2022-10-12 at 10 27 43 AM](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/16442535/195253770-9fe852cf-47f3-4527-8f55-87a9d0cde4bb.png)

Yeah, not much I can do here. You have at least these options:
- Use dots as encode symbols. So the setup should look something like this:
```lua
local map = require('mini.map')
map.setup({
  symbols = { encode = map.gen_encode_symbols.dot('4x2') }
})
```
- Try other terminal emulator and/or font. And/or OS :) 


(One of the reasons I chose these block elements as default, apart from a subjective better look, is that I thought they should be wider supported. Oh, well :( )

Dots work much better for me. Thanks.

What are your thoughts on the interaction with the explorer tree?

Is there a way to enable some color syntax based highlighting? If not, is there a plan to add it?

> Seems to work fine with Kitty, though the interaction with NvimTree still seems a bit wonky ![Screenshot 2022-10-12 at 10 34 24 AM](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/16442535/195254603-f636cbf8-794e-471c-85ce-36a050e07996.png)
> 
> I think ideally the map should offset the tree or get offsetted by it instead of getting overlapped

Unfortunately, that is by design. It uses floating window instead of a regular one. It means it is independent of what is displayed underneath it. You can set 'winblend' option in setup to 100, but it will only help in empty areas of map window.

Having it automatically offset based on what is underneath is problematic, because there is no definitive way of setting this up in a way that will recognize all "important" underneath buffers.

There is an approach of creating new `side_offset` option, but this is not very sustainable, as it won't update on window updates.

What I would suggest as a solution here, is to create/modify mappings for opening 'nvim-tree': opening should open tree and close map, closing - close tree and open map. Instead of open/close map it can be refreshing with setting proper side.

> Is there a way to enable some color syntax based highlighting? If not, is there a plan to add it?

If you mean colorize map lines based on character colors in source buffer, then yes, I would really love to implement this. However, there is no way of doing this reliably in current version of Neovim (if ever). Once it is implemented (and I have a vague desire to dive into this some day), I'll add it to 'mini.map'.

Cheers!
Thanks for the input. I'll keep using the map, works fine for me with the nuances at the moment.

There is an unfortunate cursor position issue. When cycling windows (`C-w C-w`), focus jumps to the map window, and the cursor position is always at the top, which then changes cursor position in the original window to the top. So, when cycling windows, the buffer always gets scrolled to the top.

Perhaps `CursorMoved, CursorMovedI` could change position in the map window too?

> There is an unfortunate cursor position issue. When cycling windows (`C-w C-w`), focus jumps to the map window, and the cursor position is always at the top, which then changes cursor position in the original window to the top. So, when cycling windows, the buffer always gets scrolled to the top.
> 
> Perhaps `CursorMoved, CursorMovedI` could change position in the map window too?

Oh, wow! I thought that the only way to focus this window was through `MiniMap.toggle_focus()`. Somehow, I didn't know about `<C-w><C-w>`, so thanks for that!

Yes, this definitely should be fixed. I think I'll go with adding another buffer local autocommand, though (like on `BufEnter`). I hope to fix it tomorrow.

(By the way, by default nothing is done in Insert mode for performance reasons, so `CursorMovedI` was not needed there).

For me, the experience has been great. I just miss having the option to start the mini-map with Neovim. I don't find it interesting to have to be opening and closing it, since in the end it is a quick access map.
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/54215258/195450181-6e299f02-ebbf-4139-8259-b32632c4aefc.png)

Two things I noticed:

1. Is there a way to prevent `wincmd` window switching from switch into the tree window?  I find myself switching between code windows and unintentionally ending up in the minimap window, which I don't want.
2. Is there a way to change the highlight group of the background and text in the mini map WITHOUT changing the background/text in all other floating windows?

Loving this plugin so far besides these little nits!

>     1. Is there a way to prevent `wincmd` window switching from switch into the tree window?  I find myself switching between code windows and unintentionally ending up in the minimap window, which I don't want.

I did this in https://github.com/assistcontrol/vim/blob/main/lua/aw/functions.lua#L57. It jumps windows with a configurable skip list.

> There is an unfortunate cursor position issue. When cycling windows (C-w C-w), focus jumps to the map window, and the cursor position is always at the top, which then changes cursor position in the original window to the top. So, when cycling windows, the buffer always gets scrolled to the top.

@assistcontrol, this should be fixed on latest `main`. Now cursor is set on window local `BufEnter`. Also solution to your request enabled other small quality of usage improvement: no cursor in source window doesn't change if just focused on map window. So thanks twice for suggestion!

>     1. Is there a way to prevent `wincmd` window switching from switch into the tree window?  I find myself switching between code windows and unintentionally ending up in the minimap window, which I don't want.

@kovasap, there is a way to make floating window(s) not focusable. Unfortunately, this will also made them unfocusable for mouse clicks, which is not good. I am contemplating adding another `config.window.focusable` option for users to decide what they want. Not a fan of many options, but this might be worthwhile. Need to think a bit about it. 
 
>     2. Is there a way to change the highlight group of the background and text in the mini map WITHOUT changing the background/text in all other floating windows?

~~There is a way for me to implement it in latest Neovim 0.8 (via `nvim_win_set_hl_ns()`), but this plugin needs to be compatible with Neovim>=0.6. There is a `winhighlight` window-local option which should do the trick, but quick experiments didn't work out. I'll investigate it further. I see this as a new highlight group `MiniMapNormal`, which you will be able to redefine like any other highlight groups.~~

Should be possible with latest `main` via `MiniMapNormal` highlight group.

> For me, the experience has been great. I just miss having the option to start the mini-map with Neovim. I don't find it interesting to have to be opening and closing it, since in the end it is a quick access map.

@CleoMenezesJr, yeah, of course, it is reasonable to want it to autoopen. The reason why it is not done inside module is [described in documentation](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/89c77d220f546782f1da12fe451c6a56c479ffd4/doc/mini-map.txt#L59-L70). Basically the same reasoning as to why I don't want to add `filetype_disable` to configs: too many user scenarios to cover.

For example, I use 'mini.starter' and don't want map window to appear in Starter buffer, but rather after it. So I remapped `<CR>` in the buffer.

~~**However**, I assumed adding `MiniMap.open()` call on `VimEnter` event should work. But I can't make it happen... Need to investigate further to make a more reliable advice on how to autoopen. Any input is welcome here.~~

Yep, everything works here (I was using wrong initialization order). So the general recommended approach for autoopening stays as documented: add autocommand for `VimEnter` event. So your config should look something like this:
```lua
-- Don't lazy load this!
require('mini.map').setup()

-- Use Vimscript or Lua autocommand creation based on your preference
vim.cmd('au VimEnter * lua MiniMap.open()')
```

If you use some kind of start screen, the idea is to find a way to call `MiniMap.open()` after start screen is no longer needed. See [this approach](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/89c77d220f546782f1da12fe451c6a56c479ffd4/doc/mini-map.txt#L62-L70) for 'mini.starter'.

Does this solve your problem?

That's work out of the box! It's one of the most eye candy plugins.
Tysm!
Something I've just noticed is that when setting `show_integration_count = false` the padding is collapsed because that column disappears. Would be great if that remained consistent, I think.

> Something I've just noticed is that when setting show_integration_count = false the padding is collapsed because that column disappears. Would be great if that remained consistent, I think.

That is intentional to allow users to save space or increase width of actual map content. If you want padding, add it to scrollbar symbols. In your case it seems to be something like this:

```lua
...
symbols = { scroll_line = '▶ ', scroll_view = '┃ ' },
window = { show_integration_count = false },
...
```
@echasnovski Cool. It was enough for me to add `symbols = { scroll_line = '▶ ' }` - everything shifted back over. Thanks!
The 'mini.map' is now out of beta-testing after the release of version 0.6.0. Thank you all for your input!
